## Overview

All versions and library aliases live in `gradle/libs.versions.toml`. Never hardcode a version in a build file. The `libs.*` type-safe accessor is auto-generated by Gradle after sync.

## Naming rules (strictly enforced)

- An alias must NOT share a prefix with another alias when separated by `-`.
  - ✅ `retrofit-core` and `retrofit-gson`
  - ❌ `retrofit` and `retrofit-gson` (prefix collision breaks accessor generation)
- Use `androidx-` prefix for all AndroidX artifacts.
- BOM-managed artifacts (Compose) omit `version` / `version.ref`.
- Plugin aliases go in `[plugins]`, not `[libraries]`.

## Steps

### 1. Add version to `[versions]` (skip for BOM-managed artifacts)

```toml
[versions]
myLibrary = "1.2.3"
```

### 2. Add library entry to `[libraries]`

```toml
[libraries]
my-library-core = { module = "com.example:library-core", version.ref = "myLibrary" }
my-library-extras = { module = "com.example:library-extras", version.ref = "myLibrary" }
```

Dashes in the alias become dots in the accessor: `libs.my.library.core`.

### 3. Sync Gradle

Run **Gradle Sync** in Android Studio, or `./gradlew help` from the terminal. The accessor is generated automatically.

### 4. Add to the relevant module's `build.gradle.kts`

```kotlin
dependencies {
    implementation(libs.my.library.core)
    implementation(libs.my.library.extras)
}
```

## Constraints

- `compileSdk`, `minSdk`, `targetSdk` are set centrally in convention plugins — never override them per-module.
- Do NOT apply `org.jetbrains.kotlin.android` manually — AGP 9.x applies it automatically.
